caption: Care costs me R5 600 a month on top of everything else. Are you looking after a parent, or do you expect to?

slides.title:
How I spend my R31 400
p/m looking after
my mom
Living in Parys
slides.body:
Female, 47
Divorced, her mother (79) lives with her
Job: Primary school principal
Net salary: R31 400 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.body: I'm paying it off while my mother lives in the room that used to be my study.

slides.title: Caregiver
slides.includes: Weekdays 7 to 4, to look after my mom while I'm at school
slides.body: I feel guilty and relieved in about equal parts. I don't talk about either.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Two adults, adult nappies, Ensure drinks, Woolies ready meals on bad days
slides.body: The nappies and drinks are R1 100 of this. The ready meals are on me.

slides.title: Medical aid & medication
slides.includes: My plan, her top-up cover, her prescriptions
slides.body: Her tablets changed twice this year. Each time the co-payment went up.

slides.title: Electricity
slides.includes: Prepaid, heater on all day for her
slides.body: She feels the cold. I'd rather pay this than argue about it.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Daughter's varsity support R3 000, Petrol R1 700, Car insurance R800, Rates & water R1 200, Phone R500, Funeral policies (hers and mine) R520, Stokvel R300
slides.body: My daughter is in her second year. The R3 000 is the line I'm proudest of and the one I'd cut last.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R31 400. People say they don't know how I manage. I manage because the number is tight, not because it's easy.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and put her care costs into their own category.

The caregiver, nappies and drinks came to R5 600 a month. I had never added it up.

No bank login needed.
